summary: CPU: account for the ~5% tree per-forward tax in bandwidth-vs-overhead terms, and determine if BV/N_PAD can scale to a 64-node tree (recompute-from-spine path)

bw.bandwidthAccounting:
Almost NONE of the ~5% tax is bandwidth. Quantified against the GB10 ceiling (273 GB/s unified LPDDR5X, the bottleneck):

WEIGHT READS — IDENTICAL cat9 vs native (M-independent, and they dominate). qwen3.6-27b-fp8 is DENSE (no MoE; intermediate_size 17408, /models/qwen3.6-27b-fp8/config.json text_config), so every forward streams the full weight set once regardless of how many rows M it verifies. Per forward: 24.383 GB fp8 block-quant layer weights (sum of /models/qwen3.6-27b-fp8/layers-*.safetensors) + 2.543 GB bf16 lm-head (vocab 248320 x hidden 5120 x 2; lm_head is in modules_to_not_convert so it stays bf16) = ~26.9 GB = ~98.6 ms pure-stream floor. The lm-head/in-proj/o-proj weights are a GEMM [M,hidden]x[hidden,vocab]: the WEIGHT is streamed ONCE per forward independent of M (only the logits OUTPUT, M x vocab x 4B, scales with M). cat9 reads the same 26.9 GB as native -> ZERO weight-bandwidth delta. This is why the regime is weight-GEMV-bound and the tax cannot be weight bytes.

ACTIVATION ROWS — cat9 has MORE rows but the byte delta is negligible. cat9 verifies 10 tree rows (tree_n=10 needle, FR13_B1_FIX3_GATE_BIND.md L137; M=9 draft + bonus) vs native MTP-5's 6 rows (root+5, FR13_B1_SPEED_TAX_ATTRIBUTION_BIND.md L135). Per-row activation traffic across all 64 layers ~8.4 MB + lm-head logits out ~0.99 MB/row = ~9.4 MB/row. cat9's extra 4 rows = ~37.5 MB = 0.137 ms at 273 GB/s — ~2% of the measured ~6.6 ms tax. The CAT10 experiment (FR13_CAT10_BIND.md L84) MEASURED +1 verify row = +2.9 ms/fwd, but that row's true byte-stream cost is only ~0.013 ms (8.4 MB act + 0.99 MB logits) — a ~220x gap, so even the per-row cost is overhead, not bytes.

GDN STATE / BANK TRAFFIC — already BELOW native, so it cannot be the tax. The replay route replaced the 36-row all-node state export (21.74 GB = 5.14x native, ~80 ms) with a 6-row replay (3.62 GB = 0.86x native, ~13 ms), vs native's ~4.2 GB. State traffic is below native per replay.

KV — full_attention is 16 of 64 layers (interval 4); B=1 decode KV reads are tiny and equal between arms (same served prefix). Not a delta.

Net: every bandwidth category is either EQUAL (weights, KV) or BELOW native (GDN state). The only M-scaling bytes (activations/logits, +37.5 MB for cat9's 4 extra rows) buy ~0.14 ms — a rounding error against the ~6.6 ms tax.
bw.overheadAccounting:
The ~5% tax is FIXED PER-FORWARD OVERHEAD that does not scale with bandwidth, evidenced directly in the nsys profiles (output/fr13_b1_profile_bind/, output/fr13_b1_traceless_speed_bind/chain_nsys/nsys_reduce.json, output/fr13_b1_fix3_gate/nsys_chain5_on/engagement_reduce.json):

GRAPH-NODE COUNT (the dominant carrier). Native MTP-5 = 14,368 CUDA graph-node events (199.6/draft); chain5 tree = 43,270 (627.1/draft) = 3.01x more graph nodes for the same 6 verify rows and the same weights (FR13_B1_PROFILE_BIND.md L92-93). cat9's tree_mtp row-shape/scheduler path materializes ~3x the graph nodes. FIX-3 (FR13_TREE_CONV_FUSED) fused the per-node conv emulation and dropped ~3,038 device graph nodes/forward (~63 per GDN layer; deltas.device_nodes_per_fwd_drop = 3037.8 in engagement_reduce.json) — this single overhead reduction moved cat9 from 1.077x to 1.030x native, i.e. saved ~7.7 ms/fwd (FR13_B1_FIX3_GATE_BIND.md L261). That ~7.7 ms came entirely from deleting graph nodes, not from moving fewer bytes — proof the tax is node/launch overhead.

KERNEL-LAUNCH / SCHEDULER PATH. cudaLaunchKernel native 37,807 vs chain5 61,836 (1.64x); cuLaunchKernel 14,112 vs 16,030 (FR13_B1_PROFILE_BIND.md L103-104). The tree path runs a per-row-padded verify (n_pad=16) over a tree-verifier row shape rather than the native MTP-5 spine path; this is the "broader tree_mtp graph/row-shape/scheduler path" the binds park on.

DtoH SYNC LATENCY (pure latency, zero bandwidth). The eager-pack committer's DtoH after the no-log collapse = 39,176 bytes across 7,598 ops taking 7.3 ms (nsys_reduce.json memcpy_rows kind2; FR13_B1_TRACELESS_SPEED_BIND.md L161-162). 39 KB at 273 GB/s is 0.00014 ms of bandwidth — the 7.3 ms is 100% per-op launch+sync latency (7,598 separate tiny DtoH each a dispatch/sync), the packed_dtoh_elems=133 committer glue. (The prior 4,017,072 B / 36.6 ms was diagnostic trace payload, not on the speed path.)

EAGER-PACK / REPLAY GLUE. FR13_EAGER_PACK committer (pack=1, layers=48, replay_batched=1) and the replay scan run eager around the captured graph; the standing read names "remaining eager committer serialization + tree-mode graph/scheduler path" as the next residual (FR13_B1_FIX3_GATE_BIND.md L290). These are CPU-side dispatch/serialization costs independent of byte volume.

NONE of these scale with memory bandwidth: we are bandwidth-bound on the 26.9 GB of weights which is identical between arms, so the 3x graph nodes / 1.6x launches / 7,598 DtoH syncs add wall-clock latency that overlaps poorly with the weight GEMVs.
bw.perForwardBudget:
Per-forward budget (greedy, /metrics decode_seconds / spec_drafts; native ref 0.2182 s/fwd, FR13_B1_FIX3_GATE_BIND.md):

- Pure weight-bandwidth floor (26.9 GB / 273 GB/s) = ~98.6 ms. Measured native is 218.2 ms = ~2.2x the floor — i.e. even native leaves ~120 ms on the table to launch/scheduler/eager overhead and imperfect M=6 GEMV efficiency. This is the weight-GEMV-bound regime: bandwidth sets the floor, fixed overhead sits on top.

- native MTP-5: ~218.2 ms/fwd (6 verify rows, 14,368 graph nodes).
- cat9 (post FIX-1/2/3): ~224.7-224.9 ms/fwd = 1.030x = TAX ~6.6-6.7 ms/fwd (10 verify rows, 43,270 graph nodes).
- chain5 (post-fix): ~222.3-224.7 ms = 1.019-1.030x = ~4.1-6.5 ms tax (6 rows, but still the tree_mtp graph/row-shape path).

Splitting the ~6.6 ms cat9 tax:
- Bandwidth-ms: ~0.14 ms (the +4 activation/logits rows, 37.5 MB) plus ~0 for weights (identical) and negative for GDN state (replay is below native). => ~0.1-0.2 ms, ~2-3% of the tax.
- Overhead-ms: ~6.4-6.5 ms (~97-98% of the tax) — the ~3x graph-node count (FIX-3 alone bought back ~7.7 ms by deleting ~3,038 nodes/fwd), 1.6x kernel launches, the 7,598-op / 7.3 ms DtoH sync latency (39 KB = 0.0001 ms of real bandwidth), and eager committer/replay glue.

Direct answer to the user: in this bandwidth-bound-on-weights regime, the 5% is NOT extra bytes. cat9 reads the same 26.9 GB of weights as native; its only extra bytes (activation rows, ~37.5 MB) cost ~0.14 ms. The ~6.6 ms tax is fixed per-forward overhead — the tree_mtp graph/row-shape/scheduler path materializing ~3x graph nodes, ~1.6x kernel launches, and thousands of tiny DtoH syncs — latency that rides on top of the (equal) weight-GEMV bandwidth floor and overlaps poorly with it.

ts.canBVfit64:
NO — no BV/num_warps combo fits a 64-node tree (N_PAD=64) spill-free in the CURRENT h_cache scan kernel (`_tree_gdn_kernel`, fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:387, h_cache `tl.zeros((N_PAD, BLOCK_V, DIM_K))` :458). The register law (FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND :28) is per-thread h_cache regs = N_PAD·BV·DIM_K/(num_warps·32), DIM_K=128, cap 255/thread:

- N_PAD=64, BV=16, warps=8 (our shipped geometry): 64·16·128/256 = 512 regs/thread = 2x over 255 → hard spill.
- N_PAD=64, BV=8,  warps=8: 64·8·128/256 = 256 → still 1 over the cap → spills.
- N_PAD=64, BV=8,  warps=16: 64·8·128/512 = 128 → fits ARITHMETICALLY, but warps=16 already mismatches native's warps=4, and BV=8≠native BV=32.
- N_PAD=64, BV=4,  warps=8: 64·4·128/256 = 128 → fits arithmetically at a degenerate tile.

Calibrating against the MEASURED ptxas (FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND :70-82): N_PAD=16/BV=16/warps=8 already measures n_regs=254 (right at the cap, 0 spill); N_PAD=16/BV=32/warps=4 measures 636 B/thread spill. The arithmetic prediction is consistently OPTIMISTIC vs measured (C0 predicted 128, measured 254), so any 64-node config the formula says is "128 regs" will in reality push past 255 and spill once the live working set (q/k/v/g/β/state_i tiles, ancestry temporaries) is added on top of h_cache. PRECISE LIMIT: at the deployed BV=16/warps=8, the largest spill-free tree is N_PAD=16 (the current cap); N_PAD=64 is a 4x-over hard spill, and the only formula-feasible 64-node configs (BV≤8 with warps≥16) abandon native's BV=32/warps=4 geometry entirely, so they cannot be the lossless-vs-native config either.
ts.bvWarpLimits:
Hard limits on aggressive BV/warp scaling in the CURRENT h_cache kernel:

1. 255 reg/thread architectural cap (GB10 sm_121). Measured: N_PAD=16/BV=16/warps=8 = 254 regs (FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND :78). h_cache is a static `tl.zeros((N_PAD,BLOCK_V,DIM_K))` fp32 accumulator (:458) that ptxas keeps in registers; over the cap it clamps to 255 and spills the overflow to "local" = off-chip LPDDR5X (the same 273 GB/s pool decode already saturates). N_PAD=64 needs 512 regs at our geometry = guaranteed spill.

2. max num_warps. Triton/CUDA practically caps a block at 32 warps (1024 threads). Even at the max warps=32, N_PAD=64/BV=16 = 64·16·128/1024 = 256 regs → STILL spills; you'd need BV=8 (128 regs) at warps=32. So warps alone cannot rescue N_PAD=64 at BV=16 — you must also shrink BV, which changes the tile.

3. Reduction-tree / BV-geometry concern — LARGELY DEFUSED. The seam binds (FR13_BF16_FP32_SEAM_SCAN_BIND) first claimed "BV reshapes the tl.sum(axis=1) reduction tree → ~1 bf16-ULP/node." But FR13_BV_GEOMETRY_NOT_THE_SEAM_BIND :64-66 and FR13_SEQ_SCANOUT_FIX :9 correct this: the `tl.sum(axis=1)` reductions (`_gdn_node_step` :379,:382, also :463) reduce over DIM_K WITHIN each V-row, so the reduction is BV-INVARIANT as long as it stays the 2-D axis=1 form — FR12 BV=16 AND native BV=32 BOTH measured RAW 0.0 vs native. So the schema's note holds: RAW 0.0 was measured at multiple geometries → changing BV here is likely safe for the reduction. The REMAINING geometry risk is warp/lane FMA SCHEDULING (ptxas), not the reduction tree, and it only matters for the BV=32/warps=4 native-match question — not for a recompute kernel that preserves the per-node tile shape.

4. Occupancy. A spilling 512-reg kernel collapses occupancy (fewer resident blocks) AND adds local-memory round-trips; on a bandwidth-bound decode that local traffic competes with the weight GEMV for the 273 GB/s. This is why the cache route is a dead end for 64 nodes even though the kernel still launches (no CUDA 701 — ptxas clamps and spills).
ts.recomputeFromSpinePath:
The recompute-from-spine route is the real way to fit 64+ nodes, and `_tree_gdn_replay_kernel` (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:546) is the existence proof: it runs with NO h_cache, "one (BLOCK_V, DIM_K) register tile per program, so the replay is spill-free at any tree size" (:587-589) — O(1) regs in tree size (~64-90 regs/thread even at BV=32/warps=4 per FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND :112). It launches at warps=8 (:843).

CRITICAL — the replay kernel is NOT directly reusable for verify. Verify needs the per-node GDN OUTPUT for EVERY tree node (out_i computed at :382, stored at :528-532 masked `i<N_ACTUAL`) — the downstream verifier consumes all N node outputs to form logits and check acceptance. The replay kernel deliberately DISCARDS out_i (:619-621: "out was already emitted by the scan ... A zero q ... out_i is discarded") and only re-publishes the accepted-path STATE to the bank. It also only walks the single committed accepted path (PATH_COLS+1 steps, :624), not all N tree branches. So replay answers a different question (durable state publish) than verify (all-node outputs). Verify does NOT need all per-node STATES co-resident — it only needs each node's output and, transiently, its parent's state to seed that node's step. That parent-state need is exactly what recompute-from-spine supplies on demand instead of from the h_cache.

Code to make the VERIFY scan h_cache-free (FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE fix #2; FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND :106-114 rank-1 RECOMPUTE):
- Replace the `h_cache` read at :462-467 (the `tl.sum(tl.where(offs_n==j, h_cache, 0.0), axis=0)` ancestor gather) with a recompute: for node i, re-walk its ancestry (already enumerated via strict_mask) from b_h0 by replaying each ancestor's rank-1 `_gdn_node_step`, producing the seed state_i, then do node i's own step and STORE out_i exactly as today (:528). Delete the `h_cache = tl.zeros(...)` (:458) and the `h_cache = tl.where(...)` writeback (:527).
- The machinery already exists: it reuses the SAME `static_range`+`tl.where(strict_mask)` ancestry pattern at :459-467 and the SAME shared `_gdn_node_step` body (:512), so it is bit-exact by construction (only the SOURCE of the seed state changes). This is a contained rewrite of the inner loop of one kernel (~30-50 lines), NOT a new kernel — the replay kernel is the proof-of-shape, not a drop-in.
- Lift the cap: delete the `if n_pad>16: raise` at :76-77 and warm the new node family (NODE_FAMILIES :11 + make_tree :54-65 need a 64-node entry; the strict/visible masks :43-51 already generalize to any n_pad).
- Cost of recompute: O(N·depth) extra rank-1 steps. FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE :13 estimates worst-case full re-walk (N=14, depth~6) at ~5-33 µs = 0.005-0.03% of a ~99 ms forward; for N=64/depth~12-15 it grows ~5-10x to ~25-300 µs — still a sliver, and it AVOIDS the 256-512 KB spill round-trip the cache route would pay.

CAVEAT (FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND :119-122): the replay kernel is BROKEN LIVE (gate-4 wiring seam, accept/event 2.02→1.58), so recompute's losslessness is a GPU OBLIGATION (re-gate RAW max_abs==0.0 at N_PAD=1 AND N_PAD=64 + ptxas spill==0), not a CPU-proven fact.
ts.speedCostAt64: A 64-node tree at B=1 STAYS bandwidth-bound on the 26.9 GB of weights (the weight GEMV/GEMM streams once, M-independent, ~98.6 ms floor / 218.2 ms native measured) — it does NOT flip to compute-bound. But the speed COST is dominated by fixed per-forward OVERHEAD (graph nodes / kernel launches / per-row lm-head GEMV), which the binds show is ~97% of the current tax. MEASURED per-verify-row tax = ~+2.9 ms/fwd at B=1 (CAT10 +1 row, FR13_CAT10_BIND :84) whose true byte cost is only ~0.013 ms (~220x overhead-to-bytes gap). A 64-row verify (~54 extra rows over cat9's 10) ≈ +54·~2-3 ms ≈ +110-160 ms/fwd → ROUGH s/fwd ≈ 0.34-0.39 ≈ 1.55-1.8x native. The recompute-from-spine walk itself adds only ~0.03-0.3 ms (negligible, FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE :13) and AVOIDS the 256-512 KB spill round-trip the cache route would pay; extra GDN state/KV traffic is small (replay publishes only the accepted path, ~+1.9 ms of activation/logits bytes). So: bandwidth-bound on weights, but per-row launch/graph-node overhead makes a literal 64-row verify ~1.5-1.8x native s/fwd — worth it only if 64 nodes buys >1.5-1.8x more accepted tokens/forward.
ts.losslessCostAt64:
64 nodes makes lossless STRICTLY WORSE, and likely self-defeating unless batch-invariance is fixed first. The chain5 finding (and the cat9-vs-chain5 contrast) is that BRANCHES carry the batch-variance argmax flips: chain5 (5-node pure SPINE, parent=[-1,0,1,2,3]) shows ~5 flips, while cat9 (9-node CATERPILLAR with branches) shows 22 flips (FR13_CAT10_BIND :91, FR13_BASELINE_RESOLVED_BIND :56 "cat9 22 flips" vs "native 3 flips"). The carrier is the per-layer ~1-bf16-ULP GDN realization diff compounding over ~48 GDN layers, amplified ~32x by the gate 1/rms (reference_diffuse_gdn_accumulation_explained, FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND :11) — every co-resident BRANCH row is an independent exposure to that diff at a different batch position.

DIRECTION/MAGNITUDE: a 64-node tree is ~6-7x more co-resident rows than cat9's 10 and far more branch rows (cat9's branch surface is small; a 64-node suffix-fusion tree is mostly branches). If flips scale roughly with branch-row count, 22 flips at cat9 → order ~100+ flips at 64 nodes (FR13_CAT10_BIND :49 already notes native_e5 vs oracle = 95 flips of cross-config trajectory drift at scale). Each branch row that flips is a potential lossless violation (per-token argmax-vs-clean-teacher; scalar accept/event hides it, per reference_scalar_metric_per_token_blindspot). And CAT10 already DEMONSTRATED the second-order trap: adding even ONE root-sibling branch row did NOT improve total accept (3.198→2.932) because the extra branch DILUTED the spine's deeper acceptance — so 64 nodes is not even guaranteed to be a net accept/speed win, while it definitely widens the lossless-flip surface. CONCLUSION: 64 nodes is self-defeating for lossless unless the batch-invariance / diffuse-GDN-accumulation carrier is driven to zero FIRST (the open seam — BV/warp geometry match to native, or the bit-exact-or-bust grind); on TODAY's pipeline a 64-node tree multiplies the 22-flip defect rather than holding it.
ts.verdict:
CAN we fit 64 nodes? CORRECTNESS-feasibly YES, via recompute-from-spine; NOT via the current cache kernel. The h_cache scan (`_tree_gdn_kernel` :387/:458) cannot hold N_PAD=64 in any sane geometry — 512 regs/thread at our BV=16/warps=8 (2x the 255 cap → hard spill), and the only formula-feasible configs (BV≤8/warps≥16) abandon native's geometry and still risk spilling once the working set is added (measured C0 already at 254 regs). The cap at :76-77 reflects this. The REAL route is recompute-from-spine: `_tree_gdn_replay_kernel` (:546) is the no-h_cache, O(1)-reg, spill-free-at-any-tree-size existence proof, but it is NOT a drop-in for verify (it discards out_i :619-621 and only walks the accepted path) — verify must produce ALL per-node outputs. The work is a contained ~30-50-line rewrite of the scan's inner ancestry loop (:459-467/:527) to replay each node's seed state from b_h0 on demand using the SAME ancestry+`_gdn_node_step` machinery (bit-exact by construction), plus deleting the :76-77 cap and warming a 64-node family (:11,:54-65). It is a GPU obligation to re-gate (RAW 0.0 at N_PAD=1 and 64, ptxas spill==0) — the replay kernel is broken live (gate-4).

AT WHAT SPEED + LOSSLESS COST: still bandwidth-bound on weights, but ~1.5-1.8x native s/fwd from ~+110-160 ms of per-verify-row launch/graph-node overhead (~+2.9 ms/row measured), recompute itself negligible. Lossless gets strictly WORSE: branches carry the batch-variance flips (chain5 spine ~5 vs cat9 branched 22), so 64 mostly-branch nodes likely pushes flips to ~100+, and CAT10 already showed adding branch rows can DILUTE total accept rather than raise it.

IS IT WORTH IT? NOT NOW. 64 nodes is FOR suffix-fusion / wider speculation (more accepted tokens/forward), but (a) it is self-defeating for lossless until the diffuse-GDN / batch-invariance carrier is driven to ~0 FIRST, and (b) it only pays for speed if it buys >1.5-1.8x more accept/event, which is unestablished and CAT10 evidence runs the other way. RECOMMENDATION: keep N_PAD≤16 / cat9 shipped; treat 64-node recompute-from-spine as the banked enabler to build ONLY after (1) the lossless carrier is fixed and (2) a drafter is shown to actually fill a wide tree with accept-positive branches. The replay/recompute machinery is the right foundation; the cap is a real wall for the cache route, not the recompute route.

verify.bandwidthClaimSound:
SOUND and profiled-backed, not asserted. Red-team confirms the load-bearing claim "weights are read once per forward regardless of M, so the tax is NOT weight bandwidth":

WEIGHT BYTES VERIFIED FROM REAL FILES (not the schema's word): `ls` sum of the 64 layers-*.safetensors = 24,382,562,592 B = 24.383 GB (exactly the schema's number); bf16 lm-head = vocab 248320 x hidden 5120 x 2 = 2.543 GB (lm_head IS in config modules_to_not_convert -> stays bf16, verified); total 26.925 GB; floor 98.6 ms at 273 GB/s. GB10 273 GB/s LPDDR5X confirmed online (lmsys, Tom's Hardware). Model is DENSE (config intermediate_size 17408, no MoE) -> the GEMM weight matrix streams once per forward; only the M x vocab logits OUTPUT scales with M. So cat9's 10 verify rows read the SAME 26.9 GB as native MTP-5's 6 rows => ZERO weight-bandwidth delta. The "tax is not weight bytes" claim is correct by construction for a dense model.

OVERHEAD ATTRIBUTION IS PROFILED, not asserted: engagement_reduce.json shows device_nodes_per_fwd_drop = 3037.8 (= 63.3/GDN layer, schema's exact figure), and FIX-3 moved cat9 1.077x -> 1.030x (~7.7 ms) by DELETING graph nodes, not moving fewer bytes. nsys_reduce.json confirms the no-log DtoH collapse to 39,176 B / 7,598 ops / 7.293 ms (39 KB = 0.0001 ms of real bandwidth => 100% per-op launch/sync latency). CAT10 +1 verify row = +2.9 ms confirmed (0.2287 - 0.2258). Graph-node count 14,368 native vs 43,270 chain5 (3.01x) and cudaLaunchKernel 1.64x are in FR13_B1_PROFILE_BIND.md.

CAVEAT (does not break the claim): the PROFILE_BIND chain5 arm ran at 1.4025x native, but that was a diagnostic-loaded boot (4 MB DtoH trace payload). The clean post-FIX-3 number is the FIX3_GATE 1.019-1.030x (s/fwd 0.2247-0.2249 vs native 0.2182), which the schema correctly uses. The ~6.6 ms cat9 tax splits ~0.14 ms bandwidth (the +4 activation/logits rows, ~37.5 MB) / ~6.4-6.5 ms overhead (~97-98%) -- that split is consistent with all profiled artifacts.
verify.scalingClaimSound:
SOUND. The recompute-from-spine path is real and the "verify needs all node states simultaneously" objection is HANDLED BY THE CODE, not waved away:

Reading _tree_gdn_kernel (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:387): the verify OUTPUT out_i is stored for EVERY node i<N_ACTUAL unconditionally at :528-532 (independent of STORE_NODE_STATES). The co-resident-states structure h_cache (:458) is read ONLY at :461-467 to fetch ANCESTOR states, strict_mask-gated (ancestors only, not arbitrary siblings). That ancestor state is exactly what recompute-from-spine regenerates by re-walking ancestry from b_h0 using the SAME static_range + tl.where(strict_mask) machinery + the SAME shared _gdn_node_step body. So verify does NOT structurally require all N node states co-resident -- holding them in h_cache is the current implementation choice, not a requirement. The replay kernel (:546, NO h_cache, one [BV,DIM_K] tile, :587-589) is the existence proof that O(1)-in-tree-size register footprint for the GDN recurrence is achievable, so the h_cache-free route is NOT blocked.

Register law independently checked: N_PAD*BV*DIM_K/(num_warps*32), cap 255; N_PAD=64/BV=16/warps=8 = 512 regs = 2x over => hard spill, matches FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND measured ptxas (C0 254 regs/0 spill at N_PAD=16; C3 636 B spill). So the CACHE kernel genuinely cannot hold 64 nodes -- the cap at :76-77 is real -- and recompute is the correct route.

HONEST CAVEATS the schema states and I confirm: (1) the recompute-FOR-VERIFY variant does NOT exist yet -- only the replay kernel does, and replay discards out_i (:618-621) and walks only the accepted path (:624), so it is the proof-of-shape, not a drop-in; the verify rewrite is a real ~30-50 line job. (2) The existing replay kernel is BROKEN LIVE (gate-4 wiring seam, accept/event 2.02->1.58, FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND :119-122), so the foundation has an unresolved bug. (3) Losslessness at 64 is a GPU OBLIGATION (re-gate RAW 0.0 at N_PAD=1 AND 64 + ptxas spill==0), CPU-only here. (4) Lossless gets strictly WORSE: branches carry batch-variance flips (chain5 5 vs cat9 22, FR13_CAT10_BIND), 64 mostly-branch nodes -> ~100+. (5) CAT10 MEASURED that adding even 1 row dropped total accept 3.198->2.932 (dilution), so 64 nodes is not even guaranteed accept-positive. All five caveats are correctly recorded, so the verdict (feasible via recompute, NOT via cache, with a real losslessness cost) is properly hedged rather than overclaimed.
verify.recommendation:
WHERE THE 5% IS: It is fixed per-forward OVERHEAD, not extra memory traffic. At B=1 you are bandwidth-bound on the 26.9 GB of model weights (24.4 GB fp8 layers + 2.5 GB bf16 lm-head), which stream ONCE per forward in this dense (non-MoE) model -- and cat9 reads the exact same 26.9 GB as native MTP-5, so there is ZERO weight-bandwidth difference. cat9's only extra bytes are its 4 extra verify rows (activations + logits, ~37.5 MB), which cost ~0.14 ms -- about 2% of the ~6.6 ms tax. The other ~98% (~6.4 ms) is overhead: the tree_mtp path materializes ~3x the CUDA graph nodes (43,270 vs 14,368, profiled), ~1.6x kernel launches, and thousands of tiny DtoH syncs (39 KB in 7,598 ops = 7.3 ms of pure launch/sync latency, ~0 actual bandwidth). The proof it is overhead: FIX-3 deleted ~3,038 graph nodes/forward and bought back ~7.7 ms -- by removing nodes, not bytes. So speeding it up further means cutting launch/scheduler/committer overhead, not reducing traffic.

CAN WE FIT 64 NODES: Yes for correctness, but NOT with today's kernel and not cheaply, and you should not do it now. The current verify kernel keeps every tree node's recurrent state in registers (h_cache), which caps the tree at 16 nodes -- 64 nodes needs ~512 registers/thread vs the 255 hardware cap = a hard spill to the same slow memory pool. The real way to fit 64 is recompute-from-spine: don't cache all states, just re-walk each node's ancestry from the spine on demand (the verify scan already only needs each node's OUTPUT plus its ancestors' states, and the existing replay kernel proves the no-cache, any-size-tree shape works). That is a contained ~30-50 line rewrite plus lifting the cap.

AT WHAT COST: (1) Engineering: the recompute-for-verify variant doesn't exist yet, and the replay kernel it would build on is currently broken live (accept/event 2.02->1.58), so it needs a real GPU re-gate (bit-exact 0.0 at 1 and 64 nodes, zero spill). (2) Speed: still bandwidth-bound on weights, but the per-verify-row overhead (~+2.9 ms/row measured) makes a literal 64-row verify roughly 1.5-1.8x native s/forward -- only worth it if 64 nodes buys MORE than 1.5-1.8x extra accepted tokens/forward, which is unproven. (3) Lossless: strictly worse -- branches carry the batch-variance argmax flips (chain5 5 vs cat9 22), so 64 mostly-branch nodes likely pushes flips to ~100+, and the CAT10 experiment already MEASURED that adding even one branch row DROPPED total accept (3.198->2.932) by diluting the spine. Recommendation: keep cat9 / N_PAD<=16 shipped; treat 64-node recompute-from-spine as a banked enabler to build only AFTER (a) the batch-variance flip carrier is driven down and (b) a drafter is shown to actually fill a wide tree with accept-positive branches.

Sources: https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2025-10-13-nvidia-dgx-spark/ ; https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/gpus/nvidia-dgx-spark-review/2
verify.issues:
Both claims hold and are backed by code/profile, not assertion. Minor accuracy notes for the record (none overturn the verdict):

1. The BANDWIDTH schema's per-forward narrative is sound, but note FR13_B1_PROFILE_BIND.md's chain5 arm runs at 1.4025x native (0.304 s/fwd) -- that is the DIAGNOSTIC-LOADED boot (4 MB DtoH trace payload). The clean post-FIX-3 cat9 number is 1.030x (FR13_B1_FIX3_GATE_BIND.md, s/fwd 0.2247-0.2249 vs native 0.2182). The schema correctly cites the clean number for the ~6.6 ms tax; a reader skimming PROFILE_BIND alone could mistake 1.40x for the real tax. Speed verdicts must use the no-log clean boots.

2. Weight floor: 26.925 GB / 273 GB/s = 98.6 ms using GB-as-10^9. In GiB (25.08 GiB) at 273 GiB/s the floor is ~91.9 ms. The 273 figure is vendor-quoted GB/s (10^9), so 98.6 ms is the right convention. Real measured native is 218.2 ms = ~2.2x the floor, i.e. native itself leaves ~120 ms to launch/scheduler overhead and imperfect M=6 GEMV efficiency -- the tree tax rides on top of that, consistent with the overhead attribution.

3. SCALING: the 1.5-1.8x-at-64-rows speed figure and the ">1.5-1.8x more accept to be worth it" framing are ROUGH extrapolations from the measured +2.9 ms/row (CAT10), correctly labeled as estimates, not measured. The 64-node feasibility is sound-in-principle but carries FOUR un-discharged GPU obligations (recompute-verify variant not written; replay kernel broken live at gate-4; RAW-0.0 re-gate at N_PAD=1 and 64 + zero-spill un-run; lossless flip-count un-measured at 64). The schema states all four. So 64 nodes is correctly characterized as a banked enabler, not a ready capability.

4. The dense-model premise (weights read once regardless of M) is the linchpin of the whole bandwidth argument and was independently verified from config (intermediate_size 17408, no MoE/expert keys, lm_head bf16 in modules_to_not_convert). If the model were MoE this conclusion could shift, but it is not.
